comment: Sex is a story, not an action.
A quickie in an alley is one stage and it is over. Sex at home has a prelude,
a middle and a finish, and each of those is a ROLE that many different
animations can fill -- a prelude might be a handjob, a blowjob or cunnilingus,
and which one happens should depend on what the packs can supply, not on the
That is why a stage carries TAGS rather than a position id. AAF's
ChangePosition takes includeTags/excludeTags and picks the animation itself,
so a scenario written here works with whatever packs are installed instead of
only with the pack it was written against.
AAF has its own staging system -- positionTreeData -- and it is not this. A
tree chains specific positions from ONE pack and is authored by that pack; ten
tree files exist across this whole install. A scenario is narrative and
pack-agnostic. Both can coexist: a stage may name a tree if a pack has a good
WHO CHOOSES: not Rapport. The framework executes a scenario an addon names.
Rapport's own scheduler names one only because it is standing in for Chemistry
until Chemistry exists, and that stand-in is marked as such in the code.
comment_stages: seconds  how long this stage runs. The plugin holds the clock, the same one
that stops a scene, because AAF does not enforce durations.
include  tags AAF may choose from for this stage. Any one of them.
exclude  tags AAF must avoid -- furniture it cannot use, acts that do not
belong in this moment.
handover true means this stage asks AAF for NOTHING and lets whatever is
already playing carry on. AAF's packs ship position trees -- 85 here,
22 ending in an explicit Climax branch -- and a position that declares
one walks its own stages on the pack author's timings, ending in a real
orgasm animation. Our stage clock was cutting those off. A climax also
cannot be requested: UAP hides every standalone climax position and
nulls its animation, deliberately, because the tree is the way there.
So the last stage stops asking, keeps the face and the aftermath, and
lets AAF finish the story. Costs nothing when there is no tree.
face     the Rapport expression set for this stage. Expressions follow the
STORY now, not a percentage of the clock: a percentage cannot know
that 40% of this scene is still foreplay.
A stage whose tags match nothing installed is SKIPPED, not substituted and not
fatal. A story missing its prelude is still a story. Rapport indexes every
tag the installed packs use at startup, so the skip is decided before the
scene begins rather than showing up as a stall.
